ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: For trapezoid QRST, M and P are midpoints of the legs. If QR = 16, PM = 12, and TS = 4x, find x.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows trapezoid QRST. QR is the top horizontal base and TS is the bottom horizontal base, so QR and TS are parallel. Point P lies on leg QT, and point M lies on leg RS. Segment PM connects P and M across the trapezoid and is parallel to the bases. Reasoning: Since M and P are midpoints of the legs, PM is the trapezoid midsegment. By the trapezoid midsegment theorem, PM = (QR + TS) / 2. Substitute QR = 16, PM = 12, and TS = 4x: 12 = (16 + 4x) / 2. Multiply both sides by 2: 24 = 16 + 4x. Subtract 16: 8 = 4x. Divide by 4: x = 2.

method.method_draft: Model the trapezoid using horizontal coordinates. From the diagram, take QR and TS as horizontal parallel bases. Let the top base length be 16 and the bottom base length be 4x. Because P and M are midpoints of the legs, the segment PM lies halfway along both nonparallel sides. At the halfway level of a trapezoid, the horizontal cross-section length is the linear average of the top and bottom base lengths. Therefore PM = 16 + half of the change from 16 to 4x, equivalently PM = (16 + 4x) / 2. Substitute PM = 12 and solve: 12 = (16 + 4x) / 2, giving x = 2.
